objectClass.notes: Static monumental landmark building, exterior shell only. No interior geometry: a prop kit is only ever looked at from outside, so an interior costs draw calls, geometries and VRAM for something nobody sees. Nothing moves, so one root pivot and zero sockets is the correct contract. An Isan ruin, and the registry notes are unusually specific about what that means: it is authored as partly collapsed with fallen blocks on the platform rather than as an intact building, because ruination is the state it is actually found in and is what distinguishes it. A red laterite platform with a low enclosure wall standing inside its edge and one shallow stair; a squat redented sandstone tower on a plinth course, with a colonnetted door aedicule on each face under a pointed pediment; a three-band entablature flaring wider than the body; two roof tiers each carrying a miniature aedicule per face and corner acroteria; a broken top ring; and thirty blocks lying where they fell. It is deliberately a separate asset from the Thai prang: squat, dark and rough where the prang is tall, slim, pale and encrusted.

reasoning: The identity is RUINATION, and ruination has to be geometry: a partial top ring with one corner gone, the acroterion of that corner missing below it, and thirty blocks lying on the ring, the ledges and the platform.
The plan is redented, so every slab is one closed twenty-point polygon rather than crossed boxes -- correct shape, and no interior coincidence either.

The surface is the second half of the identity and it is where the first build failed: the plate's two stones are coursed, the laterite is pitted, and the sandstone is streaked black and crusted orange. All of it is three post-construction canvas tiles on the measured materials, not a texture set.
Repetition is four-fold on the doors and thirty-fold on the debris, and all of it is instanced. The debris system is the whole difference between a building and a ruin and it costs one call.
Action readiness is minimal: static landmark geometry, box collider, and explicitly NOT breakable -- the collapse is modelled in, and the prop does not come apart further at runtime.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Three repetition systems against a ceiling of sixteen draw calls and SIXTEEN unique geometries. Thirty fallen blocks as separate meshes would be thirty geometries on their own -- over the ceiling before the building exists -- so they are one InstancedMesh with authored transforms.

ONE open doorway, on the same face as the stair. A Khmer sanctuary has a single cell and false doors on the other three faces -- that is a genuine feature and not an omission -- and the plate shows exactly this, with the stair leading to the open face.

The door surround is authored as its SILHOUETTE PARTS -- ringed colonnettes, jambs, lintel, pointed pediment, threshold -- and not as carving. The lintel relief and the naga frame of the pediment are below the resolvable band at prop distance.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 12.00 x 9.00 x 12.00 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=16000 triangles, <=16 draw calls, <=16 materials, <=16 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot and zero sockets; box collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

coordinateFrame.notes: Origin base-center as the asset declares, +Y up. The prop is four-fold symmetric except for the stair, the one open doorway and the collapse, which are on fixed elevations: stair and doorway on +Z, the fallen corner at (+X, -Z). silhouette.description: A stepped laterite platform to 1.20 m with an enclosure wall to 2.05 m standing inside its edge, a plinth course to 1.55, a squat redented sandstone tower 5.5 m across to 4.85 m, a three-band entablature flaring to 7.0 m across between 4.85 and 6.30, a first tier to 7.30 with a cap ledge to 7.55, a second tier to 8.30, a partial top ring to 8.70, and a heap of blocks reaching 9.00 m. The silhouette events are the enclosure, the flare of the entablature, and above all the BROKEN outline of the top -- an intact tier would read as a different building.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: x and z both span -6.00..+6.00 = 12.00, set by the bottom laterite slab. y spans 0.00 to exactly 9.00, and what sets the top is a FALLEN BLOCK -- the first entry of the authored placement list, lying flat on the broken ring's top at 8.70 with a 0.30 m thickness, so its upper face is at 9.00 by construction rather than by nudging. The first build spent three passes finding which hashed block was setting the height; this build authors every block's position, rotation and scale explicitly so the height is a number written down, not found.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate normalises to w:h:d = 1 : 0.850 : 1.130 against the declared 1 : 0.750 : 1.000. Area-weighted band comparison after this rebuild gives mean |delta width| 0.041 and |delta depth| 0.057 of height (first build 0.053 / 0.071), with one band past the 0.12 flag: band 2 at +0.137 / +0.316, which is the enclosure wall -- 10.8 m across here against the proxy's 9.2 m on a 10.2 m platform, i.e. the same 13% declared-aspect residual as band 0 (9.2 x 12/10.2 = 10.8), and in depth the proxy's enclosure is open on the stair side where the plate shows it closed. The first build was wrong in the opposite way from its own notes: bands 3-4 were 0.08 H too WIDE (a 6.0 m body plus deep aedicules against the proxy's 5.65 m) and bands 6-7 0.08 H too NARROW (two thin cornice bands where the proxy flares to 6.6 m). Body to 5.5 m, entablature to 7.0 m starting at 4.85, and the door surrounds pulled in, closed both.

viewEvidence.note: NOT DIRECTLY OBSERVED, and the lowest rear-view confidence of the monumental set. The tower is four-fold symmetric, but a RUIN is not: which corners have fallen and where the blocks lie on the unseen side is unknowable from one view, and the far side is authored as a plausible continuation rather than a measurement.

repetitionSystems.zFightingNote: The whole set is SUNK to y=1.02, below the platform top at 1.20. repetitionSystems.name: Blind door panels

repetitionSystems.zFightingNote: Each leaf stands 0.10 m PROUD of the wall between the jambs with a central rib 0.06 m prouder again. repetitionSystems.name: Fallen blocks

placement.note: Ten on the truncated top (six on the broken ring, four heaped inside it), three slid down the ledges under the fallen corner, fifteen on the platform floor including one leaning on the enclosure and one stacked on another, two up on the enclosure wall; every transform authored.

repetitionSystems.rationale: This is the component that makes the prop a ruin rather than a building, and it costs ONE draw call and ONE geometry. As thirty meshes it would exceed the sixteen-geometry ceiling on its own, before the building existed.

reviewHistory.summary: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.87 -- not a pass self-score. 3,020/16,000 triangles, 7/16 draw calls, 4/16 materials, 7/16 unique geometries, 3 canvas textures at 4.0 MB, factory ~80 ms. Every fallen block passes the four-corner raycast support check.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the hero2x class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: Four components and three repetition systems: 7 of 16. The platform alone folds thirteen parts into one submission, the tower folds fourteen, and the fallen-block system folds thirty into another.

materials.note: sandstone covers the tower, the broken tier, the door aedicules AND the blind panels -- four consumers, one material. Four of sixteen materials, twelve in hand.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 3,020 of 16,000. The colonnettes are the only curved thing on the prop -- eight ten-segment cylinders per door unit -- and the rest is boxes and extruded plans. The scarce axis is UNIQUE GEOMETRIES at 7 of 16, which is why the thirty fallen blocks are one instanced geometry.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: Extrusions of closed plans and boxes, plus one pediment profile extruded along Z and the colonnette cylinders. The redented plan is a twenty-point polygon and the notched platform plan an eight-point one; both are single closed shapes rather than crossed boxes, which is both the correct shape and the only construction with no interior coincidence.

Three InstancedMesh systems carry 37 of the prop's discrete parts. The fallen-block system is the important one: thirty instances, each with its own authored rotation, non-uniform scale and measured tone, at one geometry and one draw call.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.

Every material is declared textureless to the GENERATOR -- no five-canvas procedural set. Three Canvas 2D tiles (laterite coursing and pitting; sandstone ashlar, black streaks and lichen; rubble mottle) are drawn post-construction as a few hundred Path2D fills at 512 px each and bound as map and bumpMap, ~20 ms in total inside a factory that builds in ~80 ms. Every tone on them is a display-space ratio of the material's measured colour. The sandstone is re-based to its lichen envelope so the crust can be BRIGHTER than the stone, and the ledge tops carry the crust tint on their vertex colour by normal.

risks.description: Which corners have fallen and where blocks lie on the unseen side is authored, not observed. This is the lowest rear-view confidence in the monumental set at 0.55.
risks.mitigation: A tower is four-fold symmetric but a RUIN is not, so symmetry cannot close the gap the way it does on the chedi. The far side is authored as a plausible continuation of the observed pattern and is recorded as such rather than presented as measurement.

risks.description: The lintel relief and the pediment's naga frame are absent; the door surround carries its silhouette parts (colonnettes, jambs, lintel, pediment) only.
risks.mitigation: Below the resolvable band at prop distance. The colonnettes and the pointed pediment are what the eye reads at the distance a level is played from.

risks.description: A repeating tile puts lichen patches at one density on every face, where the plate concentrates the crust on the ledges.
risks.mitigation: The ledge tops carry a warm crust tint by vertex normal, and the tile density is set from the faces rather than the ledges so the sides are not over-crusted.

risks.description: The black weathering ships at 0.58 of the clean stone against a measured 0.42.
risks.mitigation: Forced by the luma-only silhouette gate: a shaded face at ~70 times 0.42 lands under the backdrop's 58 and reads as a hole. Turntable gate at four azimuths reports zero enclosed-background pixels at the shipped value.

risks.description: The cell interior ships at #4E4740 rather than its measured #0C0904.
risks.mitigation: Forced by a luma-only background test on an opening ENCLOSED by the prop's own outline. Recorded with the measurement it departs from and with its margin: luma 72 against a backdrop of 58.
